issues.description: The authors state in the introduction that the intervention will be placed before the collaborative recall phase, but the procedure section clearly places the intervention in the third phase, which is after the collaborative recall. This is a fundamental contradiction regarding the experimental timeline.
issues.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase

issues.description: The design section claims that discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced. However, the procedure section states that all pairs will discuss the exact same set of four critical details. If all pairs discuss the same items, item memorability/difficulty is perfectly confounded with the experimental manipulation (discussed vs. non-discussed).
issues.quote: discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced. [...] In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase.

issues.description: The procedure section states the final memory test will consist of 20 open-ended questions, but the analysis plan states it will use a two-alternative forced-choice format. This contradiction makes it impossible to evaluate the dependent variable and the proposed scoring methods.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions [...] In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: The analysis plan provides contradictory rules for scoring misinformation exposure. It first states that if a partner provides a correct answer or says 'don't know', it will not be classified as misleading. However, the very next paragraph states that all discussed items will be categorized as having contained misinformation.
issues.quote: However, if the partner provided an answer consistent with what the participant had seen... the situation will not be classified as misleading. [...] we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation

issues.description: Participants are tested in pairs and interact during the collaborative recall phase, meaning their final memory scores are not independent. The planned ANOVA and power analysis assume independent observations, which violates statistical assumptions and will inflate Type I error rates. The analysis must account for the dyadic structure (e.g., using multilevel modeling or analyzing at the dyad level).
issues.quote: The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA, with one within-subjects factor with two levels (discussed vs. non-discussed items) and one between-subjects factor with four levels

issues.description: The Extended Warning intervention explicitly informs participants that their partner saw a different version of the movie and explains the deception. This completely unblinds the MORI manipulation for this group only, fundamentally changing the nature of the memory task compared to the other groups who still believe they saw the same movie. This is a massive confound that invalidates group comparisons.
issues.quote: Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied

issues.description: The 'Demonstration and motivation' group completes a DRM task (listening to 4 lists, writing words, receiving feedback) plus a podcast, whereas the other groups only listen to a 7-minute podcast. This difference in task duration confounds the intervention type with the retention interval between the collaborative recall and the final memory test.
issues.quote: Participants in the DRM group will be given the DRM procedure with feedback... Afterwards, the participants will be motivated to resist illegitimate influences

issues.description: The authors hypothesize that their interventions will be more effective for participants who are aware of discrepancies between the original information and the misinformation. However, they do not include any measure of discrepancy awareness in their procedure or analysis plan, making it impossible to test this core theoretical mechanism.
issues.quote: Thus, we expect that effectiveness of our methods will be higher among people aware of discrepancies between the original information and misinformation than among those unaware of such discrepancies.

issues.description: The authors calculate a random-effects joint effect size using only two studies with vastly different effect sizes (g = 1.92 and g = 0.38). A random-effects meta-analysis with k=2 is highly unreliable and inappropriate for estimating a true effect size for a power calculation.
issues.quote: Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.description: The authors plan to run separate ANOVAs on four indices derived from the memory test: correct answers, misinformation answers, other answers, and overall answers. These variables are linearly dependent (correct + misinformation + other = overall), making separate ANOVAs redundant and statistically flawed without multivariate approaches or corrections for multiple comparisons.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test’s scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA), using all four indices: the number of correct answers, number of answers consistent with misinformation, other answers, and the overall number of answers.

issues.description: The procedure states that participants will rate their subjective certainty for each answer on a scale from 0% to 100%. However, the analysis plan completely omits any mention of how these certainty ratings will be analyzed or used.
issues.quote: Moreover, for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty).

issues.description: The exclusion criteria are limited to 'technical problems,' leaving no predefined rules for handling participants who guess the MORI deception, fail to engage in the collaborative discussion, or do not fall for the DRM manipulation. This vagueness introduces researcher degrees of freedom.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: The 'Demonstration and motivation' intervention relies on participants falsely recalling critical lures in the DRM task to demonstrate their vulnerability. The protocol does not specify what happens if a participant does not recall the critical lures, which would cause the demonstration to fail and potentially undermine the intervention.
issues.quote: See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief. If so, you were fooled.

issues.description: The description of the control condition is extremely brief and lacks details about the length, format, and cognitive load of the podcast. It is unclear if it adequately controls for the time and effort required by the active interventions.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.description: The authors plan to use DRM results as a predictor of MORI results. However, the DRM procedure is only administered to one of the four groups. It is unclear how this can be used as a general predictor, and if restricted to one group, the statistical power would be substantially lower than implied.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.description: The authors claim that normative impact is 'completely ruled out' simply because the final memory test is individual. This ignores the possibility that participants may internalize the partner's response to avoid future social friction or fear that the experimenter will compare their answers, meaning normative influence can still play a role.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study

issues.description: The analysis plan categorizes all discussed items as containing misinformation, ignoring the actual content of the discussion. If a pair fails to reach an agreement or if a participant actively rejects the partner's misinformation during the 60-second discussion, treating that item as successful misinformation exposure is methodologically flawed.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented. [...] we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation

issues.description: The authors state they will use four DRM lists that produce the strongest effect based on previous research, but they do not specify which lists these are or provide a citation for them, hindering reproducibility.
issues.quote: Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.
